newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India drifts off ahead of local holiday.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India drifts off ahead of local holiday.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended easier in slow trade on Thursday amid limited support ahead of a local market holiday on Friday and continued nervousness about the country's political crisis.
But traders said they remained hopeful about a resolution of differences between the United Front coalition and the Congress party, thus avoiding the need for mid-term polls.
Indian stocks added 1.35 percent on Thursday, but traders said the GDR market had already discounted the rise on Wednesday, which was a local market holiday.
Prices were expected to track political developments on Friday, but more clarity was unlikely until Monday.
The United Front alliance is expected to announce a new leader after a meeting at 1600 GMT on Friday.
Reliance shed 53 cents to $17.50/18.50 after strong gains on Wednesday and SBI collected 15 cents to $22.15/23.15.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.35 points, or 0.45 percent, down at 77.61 points, with the premium over the local market at 21.32 percent from 25.29 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said the decline was largely expected, as stock had begun to appear on Wednesday following a steady rise in the premium in recent days.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 49.08 points to 3,696.52 on Thursday.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index shed 3.92 points to 129.82, representing a discount to the local market to 3.80 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.39 points, or 0.61 percent, down at 64.04, a premium of 32.58 percent over the local market.
